Bill.BriefDescription: Regulating certain health care devices and procedures.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to health care devices and procedures; adding a newsection to chapter 18.22 RCW; adding a new section to chapter 18.25RCW; adding a new section to chapter 18.32 RCW; adding a new section tochapter 18.36A RCW; adding a new section to chapter 18.57 RCW; addinga new section to chapter 18.71 RCW; adding a new section to chapter18.74 RCW; adding a new section to chapter 18.79 RCW; and creating anew section.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature intends to prohibit the useof those instruments and procedures that have no legitimate use for theprovision of health care. Such devices pose a risk to the public bydenying or delaying legitimate, proven methods of treatment to patientswho need it. The legislature finds that medical instruments and procedures thatmay not have accepted uses at the time of their initial release mayachieve acceptance in the medical field in the future. Thelegislature, therefore, expects that consideration shall be given tothe evolving nature of medicine as reviews of instruments andprocedures are conducted.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 18.22 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The board may adopt rules to identify those instruments,categories of instruments, procedures, or categories of procedures thatare approved or prohibited for use by a podiatric physician or surgeonfor therapeutic or diagnostic purposes. (2) Any rules must be based upon consideration of the followingfactors as applicable to any procedure, category of procedures,instrument, or category of instruments to be approved or prohibited: (a) The instruction of use of the procedure, category ofprocedures, instrument, or category of instruments at approved schoolsof podiatric medicine and surgery; (b) The scientific basis for the use of the procedure, category ofprocedures, instrument, or category of instruments; (c) Any direct and positive relationship between the procedure,category of procedures, instrument, or category of instruments andpatient care; (d) A comparison of potential risks and benefits to the patient;and (e) Other factors deemed relevant by the board. (3)(a) A podiatric physician or surgeon licensed under this chapteror manufacturer or vendor of an instrument or category of instrumentsfor treatment or diagnostic evaluation may request that the boarddetermine the classification of a procedure, category of procedures,instrument, or category of instruments not addressed by the rules. (b) The use of an instrument, category of instruments, procedure,or category of procedures that has been prohibited by the boardconstitutes unprofessional conduct under this chapter and chapter18.130 RCW.
